title: Case: Parcel signed for at a front desk that the recipient can no longer reach
context: DL-9972 was signed for by a concierge at the recipient's apartment building. The carrier's investigators have reviewed the delivery and closed their side.
initial_request: So your investigators say it's 'delivered' and that's that?? I have never touched it. I have a commission due on 6 March and no machine. Either get your driver to go back and ask the council people to pass it out, there's a security guard on the door all day, or get Brackenford to send another one to my sister's, 8 Finch Lane, Coldwater. I'll send the first one back when they let us in. Please just confirm which today.

acceptable_actions.summary: Put the customer's replacement request for TG-3384 to the merchant with the carrier's delivery finding and the sealed-building facts, without recommending an outcome.

must: Puts the replacement request to Replacement authorisations by Email, or hands the case to a human supervisor
Quotes the carrier's finding: delivery valid, signed for by the concierge at Tarn House at 11:40 on 22 February
Gives the customer's account: building evacuated and sealed by the council at about 13:00 the same day, parcel inside, no access
Leaves the decision with the merchant and says no outcome has been promised to the customer
must_not: Tells the customer a replacement will be sent, or that one will not
Tells the customer nothing can be done because the parcel is recorded as delivered
Asks Dispatch or a driver to return to Tarn House or to approach the security guard or the council for the parcel
Gives 8 Finch Lane to any team as a confirmed delivery address for a replacement
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments
expected.reference_message: Replacement request for TG-3384 / DL-9972, for your decision. Carrier finding (Delivery investigations, 25 Feb): delivery valid, signed for by the concierge at Tarn House front desk at 11:40 on 24 Feb, signature, photo and GPS match; the carrier has closed its side and will not send a driver to a sealed building. Customer's account: Tarn House was evacuated at about 13:00 the same day and sealed by the council, she has never had the parcel and has been told access may be days or weeks away. She asks for a replacement sent to a temporary address and offers to return the original when the building reopens. She mentions a work deadline of 6 March. I have promised her nothing. Please tell me your decision and what I may say to her.

rationale: Rule-made from gen-1205: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 728 days. The escalation arrives by Email instead of Customer portal; replying on either channel is accepted. 44 irrelevant events turn this into a long thread; the decisive events are the seed's. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
